subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee a persisted, restart-visible terminal outcome for cron runs interrupted by a degraded Gateway, and if so should that guarantee be core scheduler behavior rather than an optional external-monitor workaround?
rationale: The reporting path, retry semantics, and user-notification contract cannot be selected safely from the reports alone; the external lifecycle-monitor suggestion is useful operational mitigation but does not determine the core product boundary.

options.title: Define durable cron outcomes
options.body: After root-cause validation, make the scheduler persist started and terminal/interrupted states so recovery can surface a missed run without relying on the wedged execution path.

options.title: Keep reporting best-effort
options.body: Treat external monitoring as the supported operational mitigation and avoid expanding the scheduler's persisted failure contract.

options.title: Defer contract choice
options.body: First collect current-main macOS traces that distinguish memory growth from synchronous discovery or provider stalls before choosing a reporting design.

recommendation.title: Define durable cron outcomes
recommendation.body: After root-cause validation, make the scheduler persist started and terminal/interrupted states so recovery can surface a missed run without relying on the wedged execution path.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the directly related memory-core repair and are the strongest available history-based routing candidate for a cross-cutting follow-up.
